# The Courts

## By the end of today

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
You will be able to explain why a democracy needs a countermajoritarian court and how judicial review is supposed to defend the constitutional consensus rather than replace ordinary politics.
:::

## Where this fits

Losers need two things:

- A real chance to win later
- Rights that survive an electoral loss

Courts are built for the second.

## Why majorities are not enough

![Madison on democracy and republics](../../assets/madison_democracy.jfif){fig-alt="Madison contrast of pure democracy and republic" width="80%"}

## Countermajoritarian on purpose

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Life tenure and salary protection exist so judges can disappoint the current majority.
:::

## Two jobs

Constrain the executive and the legislature.

Defend the constitutional consensus.

## Constrain the other branches

![Checks among the branches](../../assets/checks_arrows.jpg){fig-alt="Diagram of checks and balances among branches" width="75%"}

## Defend the consensus

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Enumerated powers, reserved rights, and due process are supposed to outlast the last election.
:::

## Least dangerous?

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.5em;"}
Hamilton, Federalist 78: the judiciary has “neither force nor will, but merely judgment.”
:::

## Judicial review

Courts may hold acts of Congress or the executive unconstitutional.

Previewed when we limited Congress. Cases come next.

## Not a second legislature

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
The point is to keep ordinary politics inside the rules — not to run ordinary politics from the bench.
:::

## The legitimacy cost

Independence is the tool.

The cost: judges are not elected.

## Texas note — dual high courts

![Texas dual high courts](../../assets/dual_courts.jfif){fig-alt="Diagram of Texas dual high courts, Supreme Court and Court of Criminal Appeals" width="80%"}

Texas splits civil and criminal courts of last resort. Same independence logic, different map.

## Recap

- Democracies need a place where the current majority can lose
- Courts constrain force used by the other branches
- They also defend the prior constitutional settlement
- Major cases come next

## Top Hat

- T/F: Article III life tenure is designed so judges can rule against the current majority.
- MC: Judicial review is supposed to:
- Likert: “Unelected judges have too much power over ordinary policy.”
